I'm weighing whether the same failure needs another auto-fix, since the cause hasn't changed and the runbook row still applies. The FREESHIP case looks covered too, because retired codes are meant to give no discount, but I'm still unsure whether the fix changes totals for codes that are still valid.

I'm going to decide on auto-fix without verifying, since the reasoning already covers both codes. The one gap is that the investigator's follow-up wasn't recorded, so I'll note that failure, with the decision record holding my reason.

The investigator confirms that an order with SPRING15 would fail the same way at line 18. The cause, area and confidence are unchanged, so the auto-fix row still applies. I'm recording a new decision that covers SPRING15 and the FREESHIP order it also found.

arguments.reason: Re-decided after the new fact that SPRING15 was also retired. The investigator confirmed that an order with SPRING15 fails the same way: the unguarded DiscountRates[order.DiscountCode] lookup at Api/OrderTotal.cs line 18 throws KeyNotFoundException, with cause, area (code) and high confidence unchanged. This is the runbook's Decisions row for a certain crash in this method's code, auto-fix to the coder. The fix is the runbook's expected behaviour, an unknown or retired code gives no discount, so SPRING15 and the FREESHIP order 1011 the investigator also found are covered. Totals for WELCOME10, VIP20 and no-code orders must stay unchanged. Note: the investigator's follow-up answer could not be recorded with ReportInvestigation because the tool refused its calls, so that record is missing from the run.
